topics.name: Whole numbers up to 1 000 000
misconceptions: Learners think a longer number is always larger, or they leave out zeros when writing expanded form.
When rounding, they change every digit instead of only the place being rounded.

topics.name: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners forget to carry or borrow when a column adds to more than nine.
They work from left to right instead of right to left.

topics.name: Multiplication and division of whole numbers
prerequisites: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners think multiplication always makes a number bigger and division always makes it smaller.
They forget to write the remainder after dividing.

topics.name: Multiples and factors
prerequisites: Multiplication and division of whole numbers
misconceptions: Learners mix up multiples and factors.
They think 1 is not a factor of every number.

topics.name: Time
misconceptions: Learners confuse the hour and minute hands.
They think 100 minutes make an hour instead of 60.

topics.name: Common fractions
misconceptions: Learners think a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction.
They add the top and bottom numbers separately.

topics.name: Equivalent fractions
misconceptions: Learners think only the top number changes when making equivalent fractions.
They do not know that simplest form means the top and bottom cannot be divided by the same number anymore.

topics.name: Perimeter and area of rectangles and squares
misconceptions: Learners confuse perimeter with area.
They count the squares around the edge instead of inside when finding area.

topics.name: Perimeter and area of compound shapes
prerequisites: Perimeter and area of rectangles and squares
misconceptions: Learners forget to add all the outer sides for perimeter.
They double-count shared sides when finding area.

topics.name: Decimal fractions
misconceptions: Learners think 0,5 is smaller than 0,25 because 25 is bigger than 5.
They line up decimals by the first digit instead of the decimal comma.

topics.name: Two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects
misconceptions: Learners think a square is not a rectangle.
They count faces, edges and corners incorrectly because they cannot see hidden ones.

topics.name: Capacity and mass
misconceptions: Learners confuse capacity with mass.
They think a taller container always holds more liquid.

topics.name: Number patterns and number sentences
prerequisites: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
Multiplication and division of whole numbers
misconceptions: Learners think the missing number is always at the end.
They use the wrong operation when writing the number sentence.

topics.name: Money and simple budgets
prerequisites: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners forget to subtract change from the amount given.
They mix up rands and cents when adding.

topics.name: Data handling
misconceptions: Learners think the tallest bar means the most important data instead of the most frequent.
They forget to give the graph a title.

topics.name: Position and movement
misconceptions: Learners confuse left and right from their own point of view instead of the map's point of view.
They mix up north and south.

leftOut.name: Percentages
leftOut.reason: The plan states percentages are a Grade 7 topic and are not taught in Grade 5.
